item.title: About
item.description:
About

Hello! I'm Jim Lehner, a manufacturing and process improvement engineer who specializes in reducing costs and improving the quality of manufactured products. My methods combine a formal engineering education from Worcester Polytechnic Institute with a hands-on approach that leverages modern data analysis tools, including Python. I am passionate about solving complex manufacturing problems and enjoy teaching the theory, tools, and techniques that make data-driven improvement possible in the 21st century.

item.title: Book
item.description:
The Virus of Variation

Making Sense of Death and Data using Process Behavior Charts

Using the story of the 19th-century Hungarian physician, Ignaz Semmelweis, as a guide, The Virus of Variation teaches readers how to make sense of data using process behavior charts. Also known as control charts, process behavior charts are the only tool capable of making the invisible world of variation visible, allowing us to anticipate the future based on the past. This knowledge helps individuals and teams stop being reactive and start being proactive. It replaces luck with a math- and science-based methodology that reduces costs, improves quality, and, at least for Semmelweis, saves the lives of people in need.

item.title: BQI
item.description:
The Broken Quality Initiative

Helping engineers unlock the power of SPC

Most manufacturing efforts use conformance to specification as their guiding light. Rather than operate processes on-target with minimum variance—the definition of quality established by Dr. Genichi Taguchi in September 1960—quality, as defined in ISO 9000:2015 Clause 3.5.1, is defined as the degree to which a set of inherent characteristics of an object fulfills requirements.

While on its face this definition seems sensible—after all no customer in their right mind will accept product that does not fulfill requirements—it reinforces the perspective that quality is binary. It bolsters the widely held but wrong belief that the measured characteristics of parts, products, services, processes, and systems are either good or bad, conforming or nonconforming.

item.title: Contact
item.description:
Contact

Regardless of the product, project, or industry, my experience has consistently revealed the same underlying pattern: understanding variation is the key to managing the chaos of manufacturing. When we fail to understand variation, we fail to recognize that, no matter how hard we try, no two manufactured parts, assemblies, products, or services will ever be the same. Whether we like it or not, variation is always at work.

If you're done with "thinking" about how to solve manufacturing and quality problems instead of doing the work that actually eliminates them, I'm here to help. For over a century, the tools and techniques I use have been proving their utility by answering the question: Is the process predictable or unpredictable? It is time that you started benefiting from them too.

item.title: Essays
item.description:
Essays

The essays found here explore the theory and practice of data-driven problem solving in a manufacturing environment. Although the primary tool discussed in these essays is the process behavior chart (otherwise known as a control chart), success was only possible because of the time spent where the work was done. Without participating in the production process, numbers cannot be imbued with meaning and data, as intriguing as it might be, lacks the context that is necessary to facilitate world-class improvements and quality.

item.title: Presentations
item.description:
Presentations

The Challenge of Manufacturing

At its core, the challenge of manufacturing is the challenge of making parts, assemblies, and products that are, for all intents and purposes the same. This presentation explores the role that variation plays in manufacturing and presents a case for how to make sense of it using process behavior charts.

View Presentation PDF

The Definition of Quality

Ask 10 people to define quality, and you will get 10 different answers. Although these different answers will incorporate similar ideas, the differences, not the similarities, are the problem. In order to express something meaningful, a definition must be clear, specific, and operationally useful. That is, it must be built on a collective understanding. Without one, achieving organization goals becomes exceedingly difficult because meaning is not shared.

item.title: Python
item.description:
process_improvement

A Python library dedicated to process improvement

process_improvement.py is a Python library that serves as a free alternative to paid tools like Excel, Minitab, and JMP. Assuming a rudimentary knowledge of the Python programming language, the library simplifies the task of performing calculations and generating the figures that are essential for understanding variation, reducing costs, and improving quality.

item.title: Web Apps
item.description:
Web Applications

XmR Chart-it

The XmR Chart-It web app is a free to use XmR chart generating tool. It allows users to generate an XmR chart from a list of existing datasets or upload their own dataset as CSV. For those that are unfamiliar with the XmR chart, the app serves as a practical introduction to understanding variation through the lens of process behavior charts. For those familiar with it, it serves as a free alternative to pay-to-play software. Give it a try and let us know what you think!
